verdict.rationale: Hooks let users define shell commands that run automatically before or after Claude Code actions, such as auto-formatting after every file edit or linting before a commit. Beyond hooks, event-driven automation comes from MCP channels that push webhook, Telegram or Discord events into a session, automatic code review on every PR, and GitHub Actions/GitLab CI triggers, with scheduled runs as a time-based complement. Missing for 10: in-depth hook documentation (event types, matcher/rule syntax, configuration format) beyond one-line overview mentions, and independent or hands-on corroboration that event-triggered rules work as described.
